en: to a whole lot of people...
note: Finishes #3919 (slice 048) 'Word is, the killer's already taken a knife' as its note asks.

en: I wonder what kind of face the fiend has.
Me, I'm curious.
Truth is, I was painting until recently.
Then out of the blue I placed in a contest,
and everyone hailed it as a masterpiece.
After that, painting became torture.
Could I ever top the praise for my first work?
The worry just ate at me.
So I took the plunge and became a sculptor,
and suddenly art was fun again.
Now I'm able to create my work
just the way I want.
That's what I'm carving right now.
note: 'that' = a person's character showing on the face (#3913-#3915)

en: Is s-someone there
Yes
What's going on?
I didn't sense you at all...
No, never mind that.
Why have you come here at this hour?
I was interested in your work.
Suddenly I just had to see it.
I'm interested in you, too.
I've been thinking I'd like to sculpt you.
Your outward beauty is one reason, sure,
but that alone won't do for a model of mine.
It's the mystery hidden within that draws me.
Are you a good person?
Or are you an evil one?
Well, you've let yourself into a man's home
at this hour. You can hardly be a good person.
Yes, I suppose I'm not.
note: Answers 'You can hardly be a good person.'

en: Waah! Wh-what are you doing
Living on by taking others' lives like this,
I'm evil after all
aren't I...
Please, command me as you will
Ouch, there's a bruise on my back
Why would it hurt there, of all places? Really.
I shall do just as you command
I dreamt I got into a brawl.
How brutish of me, of all people.
What a lovely morning. A day like this
makes me want to work hard all day.
note: Also follows #4065 (slice 050), which should read like #3962.

en: I am not fond of mornings.
Oh dear. That is a problem.
Then you'd never be given important work.
Ah, my apologies if that sounded rude.
(Hmph... Labor? How absurd.)
Oh, we meet again.
Quite the early riser, aren't you?
So 'bad at mornings' was just modesty.
I don't know what work you do, but every day
you work so hard. You seem a diligent man.
I wish London were full of people as diligent
and refined as you, I truly do.
Could you tell me the time?
My watch has stopped.
Oh, that must be a nuisance.
It's too dark to see. Hold it up to the lamp
and have a look.
That helps. You have my thanks.
Not at all, I'm glad to be of use.
Not knowing the time is such a bother.
Without an orderly life, people
grow utterly slack.
I would have your name.
I'm nobody of any importance
My name is Justin.
I've long worked at the bank just up ahead.
Good evening. We meet again.
How are you doing?
As for me, nothing has changed.
I work away steadily, day after day.
Banking demands honesty and precision.
Why, how nice, we meet again.
You work so hard every day.
Is it not you who has it hard?
No, no. Being trusted with work is, to me,
a matter of pride.
